title: Schematic Symbol Matcher
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Clocks and Watches with AI
description: Click the hidden symbols in an LED circuit schematic to reveal each part, match drawings of real parts to their symbols, and trace the current from pin GP15 to ground.

educational.topic: Schematic symbols and reading a simple LED circuit diagram
learningObjectives: Recall the schematic symbols for a GPIO pin, a resistor, an LED, and ground.
Interpret a simple LED circuit diagram by tracing the path of the current.
Explain the job of each part in the circuit.
prerequisites: Read the Schematic Symbols and LED Basics sections of Chapter 2.

accessibility.notes: Screen-reader description provided; all controls are standard HTML elements.

controls.label: Schematic symbols
controls.description: Explore mode: reveals the name and shows the real part. Match mode: answers the question.

controls.label: Match mode / Explore
controls.description: Switches between exploring and the part-to-symbol quiz.

controls.label: Trace the current
controls.description: Moves a dot once along the current path from GP15 to ground.

controls.label: Hide labels
controls.description: Hides all revealed names (Explore mode only).

keyQuestions: Which way does the LED triangle point, and why?
What would happen to the LED if the resistor were removed?
Why must the circuit end at ground?
commonMisconceptions: Thinking the schematic shows where parts physically sit on the breadboard.
Thinking an LED works in either direction.
Thinking current is used up by the LED and does not need to return to ground.
assessmentOpportunities: Students correctly name all four symbols without help.
Students can explain why the LED symbol points from the resistor toward ground.
Students draw a correct schematic for an LED connected to a different GPIO pin.
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Clickable diagram with matching quiz and one-shot trace
